speaker: narrator
text: What if the *loudest sound* in history happened today?

speaker: narrator
text: Saturday, seven a.m. Every window in town *rattles*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay falls out of *bed*.

speaker: narrator
text: Outside, the whole street is staring at the *sky*.

speaker: narrator
text: No smoke. No fire. Just a *boom*.

speaker: boss
text: Fireworks! Who did this? Was it *you*, Jay?

speaker: hero
text: I was *asleep*!

speaker: bit
text: It wasn't fireworks. It was a *volcano*.

speaker: hero
text: We don't *have* a volcano.

speaker: bit
text: An island. Three thousand miles *away*.

speaker: bit
text: The sound took almost four hours to *get here*.

speaker: hero
text: Nothing is *that* loud.

speaker: bit
text: One thing was. *Krakatoa*. Eighteen eighty three.

speaker: bit
text: The loudest sound ever *recorded*.

speaker: bit
text: People heard it three thousand miles away.

speaker: bit
text: They thought it was a ship firing *cannons*.

speaker: bit
text: Sailors forty miles away lost their *eardrums*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Ezra steps out, holding a brass *barometer*.

speaker: scientist
text: The needle *jumped*. Air doesn't do that.

speaker: bit
text: That's the air wave. It's going around the *planet*.

speaker: bit
text: And it's coming back. From the *other side*.

speaker: hero
text: Coming back? A sound can't come *back*.

speaker: bit
text: This one can. It's a pressure wave. A *ripple*.

speaker: bit
text: In 1883, it circled Earth over *three times*.

speaker: bit
text: Barometers caught it seven times. Over *five days*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra sets the barometer on his *porch*.

speaker: scientist
text: Then we *wait*. And we count.

speaker: narrator
text: Milo grabs a pencil and makes a *chart*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle calls a press *conference*.

speaker: boss
text: It was a loud noise. It is *over*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia isn't listening. She's staring at her *phone*.

speaker: friend
text: My mom flies home *tomorrow*. Over that ocean.

speaker: hero
text: Bit? Is that *safe*?

speaker: bit
text: The airlines are watching the ash. For *now*, yes.

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. Ezra's needle twitches. *Again*.

speaker: kid
text: Lap two! The boom went all the way *around*!

speaker: narrator
text: The whole street cheers. For a *sound*.

speaker: narrator
text: But Bit is watching something *else*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. The harbor gauge just *moved*.

speaker: bit
text: In 1883, the sea felt it. Even in *England*.

speaker: bit
text: A wave is crossing the ocean. Landing at *noon*.

speaker: hero
text: A *tsunami*? Here?

speaker: bit
text: A small one. After that far, maybe *one meter*.

speaker: hero
text: One meter. That's my *waist*. That's nothing.

speaker: bit
text: A meter of moving sea can tip a *truck*.

speaker: narrator
text: Eight a.m. Jay runs to the *mayor*.

speaker: boss
text: Close the fish market? On a *Saturday*?

speaker: boss
text: A wave from a volcano we can't even *see*?

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra taps his barometer. *Lap three*.

speaker: scientist
text: You couldn't see it either. But you *heard* it.

speaker: narrator
text: The mayor doesn't *answer*.

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven a.m. The harbor is *packed*.

speaker: narrator
text: Fish stalls. Tourists. Boats coming in with the *catch*.

speaker: narrator
text: And at the very end of the pier, *Milo*.

speaker: narrator
text: Fishing rod. Headphones. *Very* loud headphones.

speaker: friend
text: Milo! MILO! He can't *hear* me.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay starts down the *pier*.

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven forty. Then the water does something *strange*.

speaker: narrator
text: It starts to *leave*.

speaker: narrator
text: The whole harbor drains. Boats sit on *sand*.

speaker: narrator
text: And the crowd walks *out* to grab the fish.

speaker: hero
text: No! Get out of there! That's the *wave*!

speaker: narrator
text: Bit taught him. When the sea leaves, it *returns*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody listens. Mayor Doyle holds up a *fish*.

speaker: boss
text: Free lunch, everybody!

speaker: narrator
text: Jay sees the old harbor *bell*.

speaker: narrator
text: He grabs the rope. And *pulls*.

speaker: narrator
text: Clang! Clang! *Clang*!

speaker: scientist
text: That bell means *run*! Up the hill! Now!

speaker: narrator
text: The old folks know that bell. They *run*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then everyone runs. Fish and *all*.

speaker: narrator
text: But Milo still has his *headphones* on.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay sprints to the end of the *pier*.

speaker: narrator
text: On the horizon, a gray line. *Growing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay yanks off the headphones. Milo *yelps*.

speaker: hero
text: Don't ask. *Run*.

speaker: narrator
text: They hit the hill steps as the water *arrives*.

speaker: narrator
text: Not a wall. A *fast, rising tide*.

speaker: narrator
text: It floods the pier. It flips the fish *stalls*.

speaker: narrator
text: From the hill, the whole town *watches*. Safe.

speaker: boss
text: I'll... buy that bell a new *rope*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. That was the small part. Look *up*.

speaker: narrator
text: Seven p.m. The sunset turns *blood red*.

speaker: narrator
text: Not orange. Not pink. *Red*. Like it's burning.

speaker: narrator
text: Somebody calls the fire *department*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three fire trucks race up the hill. Sirens *screaming*.

speaker: narrator
text: There's no fire. There's *ash*.

speaker: bit
text: Volcanic ash, high in the sky. Bending the *sunlight*.

speaker: bit
text: Krakatoa threw ash about fifty miles *up*.

speaker: bit
text: Sunsets went red all over the world. For *months*.

speaker: bit
text: New York called out fire engines. *Real* story.

speaker: hero
text: So the mayor did it *twice*. Once in history.

speaker: boss
text: I heard that.

speaker: narrator
text: Everyone laughs. Except *Nia*.

speaker: friend
text: Mom's flight left early. To beat the *ash*.

speaker: narrator
text: Flight two-twelve. Over the ocean. *Right now*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. Can you see her *plane*?

speaker: bit
text: Tracking. Thirty six thousand feet. *Steady*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia breathes out. Milo falls asleep on her *shoulder*.

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven p.m. Bit's screen flickers *orange*.

speaker: bit
text: The ash cloud moved. It's *in her path*.

speaker: bit
text: Flight two-twelve is *descending*. Fast.

speaker: friend
text: Why is it going *down*?

speaker: bit
text: Ash melts inside jet engines. Engines can *stop*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody says anything. The room is *silent*.

speaker: bit
text: Nia. Listen. This happened *before*. In 1982.

speaker: bit
text: A jumbo jet flew into volcanic ash at *night*.

speaker: bit
text: All *four* engines stopped.

speaker: bit
text: The captain said: we have a small *problem*.

speaker: hero
text: A *small* problem?

speaker: bit
text: The plane glided. Down, out of the *ash*.

speaker: bit
text: In clean air, the engines started *again*.

speaker: bit
text: Everyone on board *lived*. Two hundred sixty three.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia holds onto that like a *rope*.

speaker: friend
text: So they *glide*. And it works.

speaker: bit
text: Twenty thousand feet. Still *dropping*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra comes in with an old radio *scanner*.

speaker: scientist
text: Air traffic channels. Let's *listen*.

speaker: narrator
text: Static. Then a calm *voice*.

speaker: narrator
text: Two-twelve, engines out, *gliding*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia grabs Jay's hand. He *doesn't* let go.

speaker: bit
text: Fifteen thousand. Then the signal *stops*.

speaker: friend
text: Bit? *Bit*! Where is she?

speaker: bit
text: Low planes drop off my map. That's *normal*.

speaker: narrator
text: The scanner hisses. Nothing. *Nothing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Milo wakes up. He looks at all their *faces*.

speaker: kid
text: Is it Mom? Is Mom *okay*?

speaker: narrator
text: Nia can't answer. So Jay *does*.

speaker: hero
text: Her plane is gliding. Planes are *good* at gliding.

speaker: hero
text: In 1982, a plane did this. Everyone *lived*.

speaker: hero
text: Her pilots know about ash. They *train* for it.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay is not sure he believes *himself*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three minutes. Four. *Five*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the scanner *crackles*.

speaker: narrator
text: Two-twelve. Engine one *relit*.

speaker: narrator
text: Engine two *relit*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three. *Four*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay squeezes Nia's hand. She squeezes *back*.

speaker: narrator
text: The room *explodes*.

speaker: scientist
text: Ha! Small problem! *Small problem*!

speaker: bit
text: Signal back. Twelve thousand feet. *Climbing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Ninety minutes later, Nia's phone *rings*.

speaker: narrator
text: A crackly line. A *voice*.

speaker: friend
text: Mom? Mom, where *are* you?

speaker: narrator
text: Mom landed at a small airport. Far from *ash*.

speaker: friend
text: She says... *we had a small problem*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia laughs and cries at the same *time*.

speaker: narrator
text: Two days later, Mom's home. Milo hugs her *hard*.

speaker: narrator
text: The boom passes over town one last *time*.

speaker: kid
text: Lap seven. Same as 1883! My chart was *right*!

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle unveils a new rope for the *bell*.

speaker: boss
text: And a *siren*. Just in case.

speaker: narrator
text: For weeks, every sunset stays *red*.

speaker: narrator
text: Milo paints a face *screaming* at a red sky.

speaker: bit
text: Fun fact. Some think *The Scream* shows that sky.

speaker: bit
text: Munch painted it ten years after *Krakatoa*.

speaker: bit
text: Next summer, the north was point four degrees *cooler*.

speaker: hero
text: One volcano. And the whole planet *felt* it.

speaker: bit
text: One sound. And the whole town *listened*. Eventually.

speaker: narrator
text: That night, they all sit on the hill. *Quiet*.

speaker: friend
text: Jay. Thanks for *ringing* the bell.

speaker: hero
text: Thanks for not *letting go*.

speaker: bit
text: Can we stop having *small problems* now?

speaker: narrator
text: Follow for a new What if every day.
